reason:
The absence is real and correctly counted (7 transitions, 0 keyframes; driven at state=phone and state=desk the guest DOM carries only 8 transition-bearing elements - 7 copies of the never-firing `top` on .b-item and the .b-behindSummary hover tint), but the finding is wrong about what that absence means, wrong about the premise it rests on, and its fix is unbuildable, off-ladder and would spend the best thing in the artifact.

1) FACTUALLY WRONG ON THE PREMISE. 'The received screen offers no evidence whatsoever that it is alive rather than a screenshot' is false. The guest foot reads 'Updated 15 July 2026', and every number on the surface - the 79, the 'days', '16 days away', 'TODAY IS 16 JULY' - derives from today's date through fixture.js, so the page a guest reopens next week is a different page. The unfurl copy is written precisely to mark that difference: the card says '79 days away WHEN THIS WAS SENT' and 'It updates itself' - the sender's line the finding quotes is answered by the received screen being a smaller number tomorrow. Proof of liveness on a plan is that the count has changed, not that it faded in.

2) IT PROPOSES BREAKING A WRITTEN LAW OF THE LOCKED LANGUAGE. LANGUAGE.md, motion row, verbatim: 'Every transition. Nothing floats idly; motion answers something the reader did.' lock.md: 'Nothing bounces, nothing floats idly.' An arrival sequence on first paint answers nothing the reader did - opening a link is not an act on the measure. lock.md also locks the measure's motion by name: 'Editing is moving something nearer. The date control moves the item on the measure while you hold it, AND MOVES NOTHING ELSE.'

3) THE FIX WOULD MAKE IT WORSE, BY THE FINDING'S OWN ARGUMENT. master.html:560-567 states the reason the one compositional transition exists: 'Position is the quantity in this direction, so animating position renders the change of the quantity rather than decorating a state change.' The finding calls that motion 'the best thing in the artifact' and is right. Its meaning survives only because it is the sole exception. Staging a 7-row entrance teaches the reader that things move on this measure for reasons unrelated to time, and the stepper stops being the one moment where movement is information.

4) THE FIX IS ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE INSIDE THE DECLARED LADDER. The guest gets 7 items (measured). At the proposed 0.08s stagger the seventh row STARTS at 0.48s and, with the smallest non-zero declared duration, settles at 0.56s - nearly twice its own '0.3s total' cap. To settle 7 rows inside 0.3s the stagger must be <=0.027s, which is not on [0, 0.08, 0.14, 0.22]. No assignment of declared values satisfies the proposal's own cap; 'stagger 0.08s', 'as the rail passes it' and 'settled inside 0.3s' are three mutually exclusive constraints. Worse, a 7-step stagger silently introduces a DELAY ladder (0/.08/.16/.24/.32/.40/.48) that the lock never declared and that audit.mjs cannot see - it reads transitionDuration only (audit.mjs:400-413). 'Every value in it is already inside the declared ladders' is not true.

5) IT IS SELF-CONTRADICTORY AND UNBUILDABLE AS WRITTEN. 'Draw the rail from the today mark downward over 0.22s' cannot be done with 'opacity and the existing top only'. A 1px rail is drawn by animating height, scaleY or clip-path - the artifact's first @keyframes and its first geometric growth. The buildable version of this fix is exactly the website effect the finding says it does not want.

6) MOST OF IT PLAYS WHERE NOBODY IS LOOKING. Measured at 390x844, the flagship case: the rail runs y=391 to y=1425, so only 453px of 1034px is above the fold at first paint, and 4 of the 7 rows sit at y=913, 997, 1165 and 1333 - off screen. At 1440x960, 2 of 7 are off screen. Four of the seven staggered steps and more than half the rail draw finish before the guest could ever scroll to them. lessons.md is explicit: 'play animations inside the visible area.'

7) REGISTER. This is a document someone opens once, on a phone, while doing something else. An entrance sequence is the tell of a marketing page, and this direction's register is ink and white, enormous confidence, nothing decorative. Linear, Stripe and Vercel animate in response to input and between views; none of them stage a reveal on a shared read-only document. The direction's two ratified delight moments (DIRECTIONS.md, section B) are both tied to an act - the stepper moving the item while you hold it, and the horizon refusing to scroll away - and AGENTS.md requires delight to be catalogued for an animate-or-restrained verdict, never sprinkled.

An accurate observation of an absence is not a defect when the absence is the declared position, argued in writing, and the proposed presence violates the ladder, the lock and the visible area at once.
